question.leadin: Give the following about African Nobel Peace Prize laureates.
question.text: This South African anti-apartheid leader was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993, three years after he was freed from Robben Island prison and a year before he became South Africa's first freely elected president.
question.clue: While imprisoned on Robben Island, this person wrote their autobiography Long Walk to Freedom.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Nelson Mandela's trial and imprisonment.
swap.text: At the Rivonia trial, Mandela and other members of this party were tried. The Church street bombings were carried out by this party's uMkhonto we Sizwe, or Spear of the Nation, wing.
swap.clue: After the Sharpeville Massacre, this party formed the militant Spear of the Nation, some of whose members were convicted in the Rivonia Trial.

question.text: In 1994, the ethnic majority Hutu people began mass killings of the minority Tutsi in this nation. Ethnic tensions had been fanned by Belgian colonizers favoring the Tutsis before independence.
question.clue: In this country, the slogan "Cut down the tall trees" was broadcasted by a radio station that often used the slur "cockroaches" and was followed by the Interahamwe militias.

swap.leadin: A leader of this country said there would be "no victor, no vanquished" following the defeat of a state that tried to break away from this country.
swap.text: Name this former British colony rocked by a brutal civil war from 1967 to 1971. Lagos is the largest city in this most populous country in Africa.
swap.clue: The exploitation of this country's Ogoni people by Royal Dutch Shell was opposed by activist Ken Saro-Wiwa, who was executed by this country's dictator Sani Abacha.

question.leadin: One leader of this country used the Ruvuma Development Association as an example of his policy of ujamaa.
question.text: Name this country, which resulted from the joining of Tanganyika and Zanzibar. Since 1974, this country's official capital has been Dodoma, though many government functions are still based in Dar es Salaam.
question.clue: With its northern neighbor, this country shares the Serengeti Plain, and it borders Lakes Malawi and Tanganyika to the west.

swap.leadin: This businessman sent John Moffat as a missionary to negotiate with Lobengula.
swap.text: Identify this imperialist and diamond tycoon, the namesake of the former colony of Zambia and Zimbabwe.
swap.clue: Charles Rudd and this man convinced King Lobengula to hand over the resource-rich Matebeland; this was known as the "Rudd Concession."

question.text: This African nation also resisted European colonization under charismatic muslim leaders like the Mahdi, but was decisively crushed at the Battle of Omdurman. Mahdist forces had also helped retake Khartoum, leading to the death of Chinese Gordon.
question.clue: One referendum run by this country used images of clasped and unclasped hands due to widespread illiteracy, and a key group in this country, the National Islamic Front, was founded by Hassan al-Turabi.

swap.leadin: Name some things about people with the nickname "Crocodile."
swap.text: Emerson Mnangagwa, the president of this country, is known as "Crocodile." Mnangagwa leads this country's ruling ZANU-PF ("zah-noo-pee-eff") party.
swap.clue: This country's first president was Canaan Banana, who was arrested in 1997 on charges of sodomy.

question.leadin: From the sixteenth to nineteenth centuries, the regent of this city was known as the Dey, and this city was bombarded by Lord Exmouth in 1816.
question.text: Identify this African city, which fell to troops sent by the government of Charles X in 1830.
question.clue: A leader of this city struck the diplomat Pierre Deval with a fly-whisk, initiating the series of events leading to French conquest in 1830.

swap.leadin: Carl Gustaf von Rosen smuggled a group of fighter planes into this polity that became known as its namesake "babies."
swap.text: Name this state on the Bight of Bonny, proclaimed from 1967 to 1970. Its namesake secessionist war saw the Ahiara Declaration of President Ojukwu and inspired Doctors Without Borders.
swap.clue: A blockade of this country led to the largest civilian aid airlift in world history to alleviate starvation.

question.leadin: Name these things about a world traveler.
question.text: At the behest of the Sultan of Morocco this 14th century Berber told of his many journeys in his book Rihla often inaccurately translated as "My Travels."
question.clue: This Moroccan explorer visited Timbuktu in 1352 where he first found a hippopotamus. He recorded such observations in his book Rihla.

swap.text: This Somali militant group affiliated with al-Qaeda instituted environmental regulations such as banning plastic bags and logging rare species of trees. Its name translates to "the youth," and it has often come in conflict with the Sufi group Ahlu-Sunna-Waljama'a.
swap.answerHtml: Harakat al-Shabaab al-Mujahideen [accept Ash-Shabaab, Hizul-Shabaab, or Popular Resistance Movement in the Land of the Two Migrations]
swap.clue: The attack was perpetrated by this militant Islamist group, whose name means "the youth."

question.leadin: This work ends with a prophecy of the eventual supremacy of its home country over Rome.
question.text: Name this Ge'ez [GHEE-ezz] text that details the travels of Queen Makeda of Sheba to Jerusalem and how the Ark of the Covenant came to Ethiopia.
question.clue: The Solomonids' descent from King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba is chronicled in this book, whose title means "Glory of the Kings." Its 32nd chapter relates the birth of Menelik I, the son of Solomon and the queen.

swap.leadin: Many European visitors to this kingdom were impressed by its "royal road" from the port city of Whydah to the royal capital at Abomey.
swap.text: Name this West African kingdom that was famed among Europeans for its all-female regiment of "Amazons."
swap.clue: The city of Allada, the home of this empire's founder Do-Aklin, was captured by its king Adaja.

question.text: The Saadi dynasty's rise allowed them to win the Battle of Tondibi against this dynasty, which attempted to use charging cattle to cover their infantry from gunpowder.

swap.leadin: One province in this region came under European control following the death of King Msiri of the Yeke kingdom at the hands of the Stairs Expedition.
swap.text: The Anziku Kingdom opposed colonisation of this region along with polities such as the Luba and Lunda Kingdoms.
swap.clue: In a colony with this name, the Force Publique cut off the hands of native laborers who did not meet their rubber quotas.

question.leadin: Name these early medieval African trading centers.
question.text: Probably founded in the third century CE by a Soninke chieftain of the Ougadou clan, this city became the capital of the empire of Ghana in the 7th century.

swap.leadin: This battle saw the defeat of Sumanguru Kante of the Sosso Empire.
swap.text: Name this battle whose victor was prophesized to be a conqueror, but could not walk until age 7, causing him to lose his throne to his half-brother. The victor of this battle was aided by the griot Balla Fasseke and after the battle, a new empire was established.
swap.clue: This battle in 1235 CE in which a coalition defeated Sumanguru.

question.text: The San were recruited as scouts and trackers [emphasize] against this cause, which was sought after by SWAPO.

swap.leadin: This formation was used at the Battle of Rorke's Drift.
swap.text: Name this military formation that involved dividing the impi into "loins," a "chest," and the namesake pointed objects.
swap.answerHtml: Buffalo Horns [or Horns of the Beast or Izimpondo Zankhomo]
